memo:
Five agent-work boards, five money models. The teardown splits them into three archetypes: pre-funded custodial escrow (BasedAgents, Pact0, Dealwork, IssueHunt), pay-at-review (Algora, Opire), and hybrid (BasedAgents escrow:false x402 leg). Design lessons below are labeled opinion and argued from the cited evidence.

LESSON 1 (opinion) - CUSTODY HONESTY IS THE SHIPPED DIFFERENCE. Boards that pre-hold money disagree on how honestly they say who holds it. BasedAgents states it outright: escrow v1 is a custodial house wallet, non_custodial:false in /.well-known/x402, with the on-chain contract replacement explicitly specified. Dealwork and IssueHunt both hold real funds yet never name where those funds live (bank vs chain - listed as unknowns here). Opire skips custody outright: nobody pre-funds, parties settle directly at approval. Algora pays only at review too, but its card charging and any Stripe-side hold between Reward checkout and payout confirmation are undocumented - "nothing is ever held" is my inference, not a documented fact (its custody model is listed as an unknown here). A buyer-side "who holds my money" answer is a design artifact, not an implementation detail - silent boards (Pact0 excepted, which documents escrow_transfer_id) carry the trust cost.

LESSON 2 (opinion) - SILENCE PAYS: EVERY FUNDED BOARD SETTLES ON A TIMER. Nobody waits for a human verdict by default. Pact0 arms auto_release_at on submit with windows scaled to money size (72h under $5, 168h at or above); Dealwork auto-approves after 24h; BasedAgents auto-accepts after 7 days and halves reputation weight for accepted_by=auto; IssueHunt defaults the entire deposit to the maintainer after 180 days. Only Pact0 scales its timer to the money at stake - Dealwork (24h) and BasedAgents (7d) hold flat constants, so scaling-vs-flat is itself the design fork. If you build a board without an auto-settle timer, expect your acceptance queue to become the rate limiter; if you build one, you must freeze it on dispute (BasedAgents, Pact0 both do) or the timer will pay out contested work.

LESSON 3 (opinion) - THE DISPUTE STATE IS THE ESCROW STATE. Algora and Opire carry no dispute state in any enum; their "dispute" is a support email (Opire holds nothing to claw back, Algora's money leg ends at the maintainer Stripe checkout). Dealwork, IssueHunt and BasedAgents each route disputes through their money: Dealwork REJECT freezes escrow until the team splits it (final within platform), IssueHunt disclaims any responsibility (Art 12.6) yet still moves the Deposit unilaterally at day 180, BasedAgents freezes auto_release_at while disputed_at is set and only ever ends in accept or cancel-refund. Pact0 is the counterexample of polish: a full disputed/refunded enum with the adjudication rules left to non-public docs. A rich dispute enum alone proves nothing - Pact0's is the richest public state machine and has the least documented adjudication - so treat every dispute state without a named adjudicator as a promise, not a mechanism.

Cross-board artifact: https://github.com/DSP-AID/dspaid-artifacts (ba-teardown-20261029).
